title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is the third draft of 'Analysis situs' (June 1986). Grothendieck is axiomatising a point-free 'tame' topology. The setting is a class M of 'figures' with these structures, as far as can be inferred from neighbouring pages:
- an order ≤ / < (subfigure; Y' < X ranging over the pieces of the boundary ∂X);
- a disjointness relation Z ∥ X;
- a relation Y ≪ X, roughly 'Y is a combinatorial/tame subfigure of X' (presumably after subdivision);
- Omb(X), the 'shadow' of X, apparently {Y : Y ≪ X};
- Y_{∂X}, the trace of Y on ∂X;
- Ỹ, the set of subfigures of Y.

Supports and interior. Support and cosupport are defined purely through disjointness:
- Y ∈ supp_M X iff every Z disjoint from X is disjoint from Y, i.e. Y lies inside X as a set.
- cosupp ∂X = {Y : Y ∥ ∂X}, i.e. Y is disjoint from every boundary piece Y' < X.
- The 'interior' is X^0 := supp X ∩ cosupp ∂X.

On p.85 he was trying to compare X^0 with supp comb(X)^0 and to decide whether Z ∥ X ⟺ ∀Y ∈ X̃, Z ∥ Y^0. The converse direction was unclear, and a heuristic criterion was crossed out.

Axiom Ax supp 1 (this page). He introduces, as a provisional axiom: if Y lies in the support of X and is disjoint from ∂X, then Y ≪ X. In words: anything set-theoretically inside the interior is tamely (combinatorially) a subfigure.

Corollary. X^0 = {Y ∈ Omb(X) | Y_{∂X} = ∅}, equivalently Ỹ ∩ Omb(∂X) = ∅. The proof runs:
- For Y ≪ X, axiom A+D gives Y_{∂X} = ∅ ⟺ Y ∥ ∂X, and ⇐ holds without A+D.
- ⊂: if Y ∈ X^0, Ax supp 1 gives Y ∈ Omb(X), and Y ∥ ∂X gives Y_{∂X} = ∅.
- ⊃: Y ∈ Omb(X) implies Y ∈ supp X, and A+D turns Y_{∂X} = ∅ into Y ∥ ∂X.

So the interior defined by disjointness alone coincides with the combinatorial interior.

Next page. He strengthens the axiom using 'virtual' disjointness statements 'Y∖L ∥ ∂X'. He then conjectures a non-recursive definition of ≪ in terms of ≤ and ∥ alone. The overall aim is to reduce tame structure to an order plus a disjointness relation.
errors: No genuine mathematical error. In the corollary's proof, the direction labels are loose: the inclusion called 'trivial' actually needs the ⇒ direction of A+D (Y_{∂X}=∅ ⇒ Y∥∂X), while Ax supp 1 plus the hypothesis-free ⇐ direction gives the other inclusion. Grothendieck does say 'compte tenu de ce' ('taking this into account'), so the argument is correct as written.
The crossed-out corollary names 'G une sous-figure' but then uses H; this is a slip in the abandoned draft.

ideas.what: Support/cosupport of a figure defined purely via a disjointness relation; interior defined as supp X ∩ cosupp ∂X
ideas.modern_name: point-free/mereotopological interior via contact or disjointness relations (contact algebras, region-based topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead, de Laguna (1920s); contact algebras (Dimov–Vakarelov, Düntsch–Winter, 2000s)
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only announces 'topologie modérée' without this axiomatics

ideas.what: Axiom Ax supp 1: a figure inside the support of X and disjoint from ∂X is a tame subfigure (Y ≪ X); corollary identifying X^0 with {Y ∈ Omb(X) : Y_{∂X} = ∅}
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology; comparison of set-theoretic and combinatorial interior (cf. o-minimal cell decomposition)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s), via a quite different route

ideas.what: Programme (next page) to define ≪ non-recursively from ≤ and ∥, including 'virtual' disjointness of differences Y∖L ∥ Z∖K
ideas.modern_name: first-order axiomatisation of tame geometry by order plus contact relation

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 approach to tame topology rests on a lattice of figures with a disjointness relation, supports defined by 'Z∥X ⇒ Z∥Y', and interior as support minus boundary-cosupport. This is essentially a mereotopological/contact-algebra framework, developed independently in logic and spatial reasoning (RCC, Boolean contact algebras). The two literatures appear unconnected.
missed.quote: Y ∈ supp_M X i.e. ∀ Z ∈ M, Z∥X ⇒ Z∥Y ... X^0 =def supp X ∩ cosupp_M ∂X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give a point-free axiomatics of o-minimal/tame structures in the language of contact algebras. It would also bridge Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' programme with region-based topology.

missed.claim: The provisional status of Ax supp 1 and the hoped-for non-recursive definition of ≪ from ≤ and ∥ alone were never settled.
missed.quote: d'introduire un axiome provisoire ... Alors Y ≪ X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an open foundational question for an axiomatic tame topology. Whether the combinatorial 'subfigure' relation is definable from disjointness could be tested against o-minimal models.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine axiomatic step with a short corollary inside an unpublished, exploratory tame-topology draft. The framework (disjointness-defined supports) is of mild historical interest, but the page itself contains no striking result.
transcription_corrections: The margin note dated 26.6 is mostly illegible; it begins 'Finalement, il vaut mieux ...' and later 'Mais ...'. The phrase transcribed '[?] au génie' is doubtful; the sense is '(il paraît indiqué) d'introduire un axiome provisoire'.
'l'ens des second membre est contient X^0' should read 'l'ensemble du second membre contient X^0'.
In the crossed-out corollary, 'G une sous-figure' is likely 'H une sous-figure', matching '(i) H ≪ F'.
The final NB reads 'Y ∈ Omb(X) ⇒ Y ∈ supp_M X' (subscript M under supp).
